processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The experimental alloy Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni was melted in an induction furnace prior to solution treatment.
Solution heat-treated for 35 min at 1250 °C in a protective argon atmosphere and then water quenched; this is the defining process of this sample (state_label 'Solution Treated').
The solution-treated material was cut into 3-mm (length), 3-mm (width) and 1-mm (thickness) samples for testing.

structures.overall_structure: In the solution-treated (as-quenched) condition the Ni-containing Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni alloy has a duplex austenite (γ) + ferrite (α) microstructure, characterised as the bulk γ and α phases measured without ordered precipitates.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Nano-indentation at a constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s−1 up to a maximum load of 10000 μN with a hold time of 20 s; each measurement in a particular phase repeated at least 25 times and in arrays of 50–70 indentations.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s−1 up to a maximum load of 10000 μN with a hold time of 20 s; each measurement in a particular phase repeated at least 25 times, in arrays of 50–70 indentations
characterization_methods.purpose: determine the nano-hardness of the solution-treated γ and α phases (and of phase combinations) for the Ni-containing alloy
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated Ni-containing alloy: γ = 4.2 GPa and α = 3.1 GPa.

characterization_methods.technique: field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) with X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss Sigma Field Emission SEM operated at 20 kV, fitted with high-speed X-ray EDS; specimens polished and etched in 5% nital
characterization_methods.purpose: microstructural observation and imaging of nano-indentation indents

characterization_methods.technique: transmission electron microscopy (TEM): selected-area diffraction patterns (SADP) and bright-field (BF) imaging
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2000FX TEM; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in a mixture of 10% perchloric acid and 90% ethanol with an applied potential of 25 V
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: applied potential of 25 V for twin-jet electro-polishing
characterization_methods.purpose: characterise the ordered phases (κ-carbide and B2) in the microstructures

computational_details.simulation_method: First-principles (ab-initio) density functional theory (DFT) calculations of the ordered phases (κ-carbide and FeAl-B2) studied in both duplex low-density steels
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Ultrasoft pseudo-potentials created on a modified Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos (RRKJ) scheme; spin-polarized generalized gradient approximation (GGA) of Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) exchange-correlation functional
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Structure optimization with Brillouin-zone integration on an 18×18×18 Monkhorst-Pack grid; real-space grid with a 50 Ryd energy cut-off for charge density; augmentation charges expanded up to 600 Ryd; 30×30×30 grid with a 60 Ryd energy cut-off for electronic density of states and formation energy; Murnaghan equation of state for bulk modulus; dynamical matrices from linear response in the harmonic approximation; DOS by the tetrahedron method on a 30×30×30 mesh.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated lattice parameter of the ordered FeAl-B2 precipitate (with and without spin effects) was slightly less than the experimental value but in good agreement with reported experimental values.

analytical_models.equation_role: fit simulated unit-cell volumes to obtain the bulk modulus B0
obtain C11 = ρ·(v_l[100])^2, C44 = ρ·(v_t[100])^2, and C12 via the [111] longitudinal sound velocity
analytical_models.model_note: Longitudinal/transverse sound velocities in the [100] and [111] directions used with the compound density.

analytical_models.equation_role: volume-conserving orthorhombic and monoclinic distortions to determine (C11−C12) and C44 from total-energy changes
compute B0, anisotropy factor Cα, shear modulus G, and Young's moduli E100 and E111 from the elastic constants

unmapped_findings: For the Ni-containing Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni alloy, the solution-treated (as-quenched) state is measured as γ and α phases; nano-indentation gives ≈4.2 GPa for the solution-treated γ phase and ≈3.1 GPa for the solution-treated α phase (Table 2 'Solution Treated' row), consistent with the text's ≈4 GPa (γ) and ≈3 GPa (α) for solution-treated material.

Tables 1 and 2 label the Ni-containing alloy as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C-5Ni (0.5 C), whereas the abstract, introduction, results and methods give Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni (0.8 C); this appears to be a typographical inconsistency in the carbon content (0.5 vs 0.8).

Load–depth curves for the solution-treated Ni-containing alloy are shown in Fig. 4 (panels a and c): the α and γ solution-treated curves rise to a flat plateau at a load of ≈10000 (µN) reached at depths of roughly 200–310 nm, with near-vertical unloading branches.

The nano-indentation technique as performed cannot measure the hardness of isolated nano-sized precipitates; it yields a compound (matrix + particle) hardness value, and changing the indentation size/volume would introduce a nano-indentation size-effect — a methodological limitation stated for the study.
